key_insight: The paper introduces a deterministic way to “draw” arbitrary 2D curves and 3D shapes on water by combining focused transient waves with curve-based sampling and amplitude correction.
engineering_relevance: This enables more precise wave-field shaping for ocean engineering, with potential uses in wave control, experimental testing, and programmable surface pattern generation.
method: Parameterize target shapes with Bézier curves
Sample the curve at equal arc length to place wave foci
Use Iterative Amplitude Correction (IAC) to reduce overshoot and improve superposition
evidence_signal: The approach was validated with linear wave theory, SPH simulations, and physical FloWave basin experiments that reproduced 2D and 3D target shapes such as a star and pyramid.
watch_item: Accuracy may degrade for larger-amplitude waves because nonlinear wave effects are not yet fully incorporated.
